headline: SS troops murder Canadian prisoners at Ardenne Abbey
detail: Men of the 12th SS Panzer Division shoot captured Canadians near Caen. About 156 Canadian soldiers are murdered after capture during the Normandy campaign.

headline: Oradour-sur-Glane: 643 villagers massacred
detail: A company of the SS Das Reich division shoots the men and burns the women and children in the church. The ruins are kept as a memorial.

headline: German troops massacre the villagers of Distomo, Greece
detail: In reprisal for a partisan ambush, SS troops kill more than 200 men, women and children in the village and burn their houses.

headline: First V-1 flying bombs fall on England
detail: One hits a railway bridge at Grove Road, Bow, killing six. Over nine months V-1s will kill some 6,000 people in Britain.

headline: US Marines land on Saipan in the Marianas
detail: Two Marine divisions storm the west coast. From Saipan, Japan's home islands will lie within range of the new B-29 bombers.

headline: B-29s from China bomb Japan's home islands
detail: On the night of 15-16 June Superfortresses from bases near Chengdu attack the Yawata steelworks, the first raid on Japan since Doolittle's.

headline: Iceland proclaims itself a republic
detail: At Thingvellir, in pouring rain, Iceland ends its union with occupied Denmark and becomes an independent republic.

headline: Flying bomb hits the Guards Chapel during Sunday service
detail: A V-1 brings down the roof at Wellington Barracks, London, killing 121 soldiers and civilians, the deadliest flying-bomb strike of the war.

headline: Japan's Ichi-Go offensive takes Changsha
detail: Japan's largest land offensive of the war drives south through Hunan. Changsha, which held out three times before, falls.

headline: Battle of the Philippine Sea: the 'Marianas Turkey Shoot'
detail: American carrier pilots destroy hundreds of Japanese aircraft and submarines sink the carriers Taiho and Shokaku. Japan's naval air arm never recovers.

headline: Operation Bagration: the Red Army strikes in Belarus
detail: Three years to the day after Germany invaded, Soviet fronts attack Army Group Centre. Within weeks 28 German divisions are destroyed.

headline: Roosevelt signs the G.I. Bill
detail: The Servicemen's Readjustment Act promises veterans college tuition, low-cost home loans and unemployment pay. Millions will use it.

headline: Siege of Imphal broken as relief columns meet
detail: British and Indian troops from Kohima and Imphal meet at Milestone 109 and reopen the road. Japan's invasion of India has failed.

headline: German commander at Cherbourg surrenders
detail: General von Schlieben gives up the port, but its harbour is so thoroughly wrecked that it cannot handle Allied shipping for weeks.

headline: Red Army liberates Minsk
detail: Soviet tanks enter the Belarusian capital, trapping some 100,000 German soldiers to the east. Belarus has lost about a quarter of its people.

headline: Horthy halts the deportation of Hungary's Jews
detail: Since mid-May some 437,000 Jews have been sent from Hungary to Auschwitz, most murdered on arrival. Under international pressure the trains stop.

headline: Saipan falls; civilians leap from Marpi Point
detail: The island is declared secure after a final banzai charge. Hundreds of Japanese civilians, taught to fear capture, kill themselves and their children.

headline: Vilnius liberated by the Red Army and the Home Army
detail: Polish Home Army units fight beside Soviet troops for the city. Within days the NKVD arrests the Polish officers.

headline: Port Chicago explosion kills 320, mostly Black sailors
detail: Two ammunition ships blow up at a California naval magazine. Black sailors who later refuse to resume loading are convicted of mutiny.

headline: 57,000 German prisoners marched through Moscow
detail: Captives from the Bagration battles parade along the Garden Ring under guard. Street-cleaning trucks follow behind them.

headline: Tojo resigns as Japan's prime minister
detail: The loss of Saipan brings down General Tojo Hideki's cabinet. General Koiso Kuniaki succeeds him.

headline: Bomb at Hitler's headquarters fails to kill him
detail: Colonel Claus von Stauffenberg's briefcase bomb explodes at the Wolf's Lair. The coup in Berlin collapses; Stauffenberg is shot before midnight.

headline: American troops land on Guam
detail: US forces return to the first American territory Japan seized in 1941. The Chamorro islanders have endured two and a half years of occupation.

headline: Bretton Woods conference creates the IMF and World Bank
detail: Delegates of 44 nations meeting in New Hampshire agree the post-war monetary order, with currencies pegged to the US dollar.

headline: American 'Dixie Mission' reaches Yan'an
detail: A US observer group flies to Mao Zedong's base to assess the Communist forces fighting Japan in northern China.

headline: Red Army reaches Majdanek camp at Lublin
detail: The SS fled before destroying it; the gas chambers stand intact. About 78,000 people were murdered here, some 59,000 of them Jews.

headline: Operation Cobra: Americans break out at Saint-Lo
detail: After carpet bombing that also kills American soldiers, including General McNair, the US First Army punches through the German line.

headline: Saint-Exupery vanishes on a reconnaissance flight
detail: The author of The Little Prince takes off from Corsica in a P-38 and never returns. Wreckage is found off Marseille decades later.

headline: Warsaw Uprising begins at 17:00
detail: Some 40,000 Home Army fighters, with few weapons, rise to free the capital before the Red Army arrives.

headline: Roma family camp at Auschwitz-Birkenau liquidated
detail: On the night of 2-3 August the SS murder the last Roma and Sinti prisoners, about 4,300 people according to the Auschwitz Memorial.

headline: Myitkyina falls after a 78-day siege
detail: Chinese and American troops, including Merrill's Marauders, take the north Burma town and its airfield, opening the way for the Ledo Road.

headline: Anne Frank and her family arrested in Amsterdam
detail: Police raid the secret annexe at Prinsengracht 263. Of the eight people hidden there, only Otto Frank will survive.

headline: Wola massacre begins in Warsaw
detail: German troops and collaborator units kill between 40,000 and 50,000 civilians in the Wola district within days, house by house.

headline: Hengyang falls after a 47-day siege
detail: General Fang Xianjue's Chinese garrison holds the Hunan rail town far longer than Japan expected before it is overwhelmed.

headline: Guam declared secure
detail: Organised Japanese resistance ends. Scattered soldiers hold out in the jungle, one of them until 1972.

headline: Operation Dragoon: Allies land in Provence
detail: American and French troops come ashore between Toulon and Cannes. French Army B includes tens of thousands of soldiers from North and West Africa.

headline: Paris rises against the German garrison
detail: The police strike and seize the Prefecture; Resistance fighters build barricades across the city as the Allies approach.

headline: Falaise pocket closes
detail: Polish, Canadian and American troops seal the trap in Normandy. Tens of thousands of Germans are captured amid roads choked with wreckage.

headline: Dumbarton Oaks talks begin to plan the United Nations
detail: Delegates of the United States, Britain, the Soviet Union and China meet in Washington to draft a new world organisation.

headline: Romania changes sides
detail: King Michael has the dictator Ion Antonescu arrested and accepts Allied terms. Romania declares war on Germany two days later.

headline: Paris liberated
detail: General von Choltitz surrenders the city largely intact. At the Hotel de Ville de Gaulle praises a Paris that freed itself.

headline: Slovak National Uprising begins
detail: Slovak army units and partisans rise against the German occupation and the collaborationist state. The revolt is crushed by late October.

headline: Warsaw's Old Town falls after a month of siege
detail: Over two nights about 5,300 insurgents and civilians escape through the sewers. Wounded fighters left behind in field hospitals are murdered.

headline: Brussels liberated by the Guards Armoured Division
detail: British tanks dash more than 100 kilometres in a day to enter the Belgian capital through cheering crowds.

headline: Last transport leaves Westerbork for Auschwitz
detail: Among the 1,019 people deported are Anne Frank and her family. Of 107,000 Jews deported from the Netherlands, about 5,200 survived.

headline: Antwerp's port captured intact
detail: British 11th Armoured Division takes Europe's second port with Belgian Resistance help, but the Scheldt estuary stays in German hands.

headline: First V-2 rocket strikes London
detail: A supersonic rocket explodes in Staveley Road, Chiswick, killing three. There is no warning and no defence.

headline: Fatherland Front takes power in Bulgaria
detail: A coup in Sofia brings a Communist-led government to power as the Red Army crosses the border. Bulgaria turns on Germany.

headline: First American patrols cross into Germany
detail: Near Stolzembourg on the Luxembourg border, a US patrol becomes the first Western Allied unit to set foot on German soil.

headline: Red Army takes Praga, across the Vistula from Warsaw
detail: Soviet and Polish troops reach the east bank. On the far side the Uprising fights on; the Soviet advance halts.

headline: US Marines land on Peleliu
detail: Expected to fall in days, the island takes over two months and costs some 10,000 American casualties against defenders dug into caves.

headline: Operation Market Garden: airborne landings in Holland
detail: Some 35,000 paratroopers and glider troops land to seize the bridges as far as Arnhem on the Lower Rhine.

headline: Junyo Maru torpedoed; about 5,600 prisoners die
detail: A British submarine sinks a Japanese hell ship off Sumatra crammed with Allied POWs and Javanese forced labourers.

headline: Finland signs an armistice with the Soviet Union
detail: Finland must cede territory, pay reparations and expel German forces from its soil, which starts the Lapland War.

headline: British airborne survivors withdraw across the Rhine
detail: In rain and darkness about 2,400 men escape the Oosterbeek perimeter. More than 6,000 are left behind as prisoners.

headline: Warsaw Uprising capitulates after 63 days
detail: The Home Army surrenders with combatant rights. Some 150,000 to 200,000 civilians are dead, and Hitler orders the city razed.

headline: Sonderkommando revolt at Auschwitz-Birkenau
detail: Prisoners forced to work in the crematoria rise up and blow up Crematorium IV. Most are killed in the fighting or shot afterwards.

headline: Churchill and Stalin sketch the 'percentages' deal
detail: In Moscow, Churchill pencils spheres of influence in the Balkans on a half-sheet of paper. Stalin ticks it with a blue pencil.

headline: German troops leave Athens
detail: The occupiers pull out of a city that lost tens of thousands to famine. British troops arrive two days later.

headline: Rommel forced to take poison
detail: Implicated after the 20 July plot, the field marshal is offered suicide to spare his family. Germany is told he died of his wounds.

headline: Arrow Cross seizes power in Hungary
detail: Horthy's attempt to leave the war fails. Under Ferenc Szalasi's regime, militiamen murder Jews on the banks of the Danube in Budapest.

headline: Roosevelt recalls General Stilwell from China
detail: After a bitter feud with Chiang Kai-shek, 'Vinegar Joe' Stilwell is withdrawn and replaced by General Albert Wedemeyer.

headline: MacArthur lands on Leyte: 'I have returned'
detail: American troops land in the central Philippines. MacArthur wades ashore at Palo with President Sergio Osmena.

headline: Belgrade liberated by Partisans and the Red Army
detail: After a week of street fighting, Tito's Yugoslav Partisans and Soviet troops free the Yugoslav capital.

headline: Aachen surrenders
detail: Charlemagne's city, largely in ruins, is the first German city taken by the Western Allies.

headline: First organised kamikaze attacks at Leyte Gulf
detail: In the largest naval battle in history, Japanese pilots deliberately crash into American ships; the escort carrier St. Lo sinks.

headline: Last transport leaves Theresienstadt for Auschwitz
detail: The final train of the autumn deportations carries more than 2,000 people from the ghetto; most are murdered on arrival.

headline: Commandos land on Walcheren to open the Scheldt
detail: British commandos and Canadian troops clear the island guarding Antwerp's estuary. The Scheldt battles cost Canada over 6,000 casualties.

headline: Roosevelt wins an unprecedented fourth term
detail: He defeats Thomas Dewey. His new running mate is a Missouri senator, Harry S. Truman.

headline: Soviet spy Richard Sorge hanged in Tokyo
detail: The German journalist who warned Moscow of Barbarossa, and that Japan would not attack Siberia, is executed at Sugamo prison.

headline: Death marches of Budapest's Jews begin
detail: Tens of thousands of Jews are forced to walk toward the Austrian border to dig fortifications. Thousands die on the road.

headline: Guilin falls to Japan
detail: The Ichi-Go offensive overruns Guilin and then Liuzhou in Guangxi, with the American airbases around them.

headline: RAF Lancasters sink the battleship Tirpitz
detail: Tallboy bombs capsize the ship at her anchorage near Tromso, Norway. Around a thousand of her crew die.

headline: Leclerc's division liberates Strasbourg
detail: The tricolour flies from the cathedral, fulfilling the oath his men swore at Kufra in the Libyan desert in 1941.

headline: B-29s from the Marianas raid Tokyo
detail: 111 Superfortresses from Saipan attack an aircraft-engine plant in the first raid on Tokyo since 1942.

headline: V-2 hits Woolworths in New Cross
detail: A rocket falls on a crowded store in south-east London at lunchtime on a Saturday, killing 168 people.

headline: First Allied convoy reaches Antwerp
detail: With the Scheldt swept of mines, Liberty ships unload in the port, easing the Allies' supply crisis.

headline: Albania liberated as the Germans withdraw
detail: Communist partisans under Enver Hoxha take control of the whole country.

headline: Thiaroye: French troops fire on African veterans
detail: Near Dakar, tirailleurs freed from German camps who demand their back pay are shot down. France admits 35 dead, later 70; the true toll is unknown.

headline: Fighting erupts in Athens: the Dekemvriana
detail: Police fire on a left-wing demonstration in Syntagma Square. Weeks of street fighting follow between ELAS and British and Greek government forces.

headline: Palawan massacre of American prisoners
detail: Fearing rescue, Japanese guards herd about 150 American POWs into air-raid shelters, douse them with petrol and set them alight. Eleven escape.

headline: Glenn Miller's plane disappears over the Channel
detail: The bandleader, flying to Paris to play for the troops, is never found.

headline: Chinese troops take Bhamo in northern Burma
detail: After a month-long siege, Sun Li-jen's 38th Division captures the town, clearing the route for the Ledo Road.

headline: Germany attacks in the Ardennes
detail: Three German armies strike thinly held American lines in fog and snow. The Battle of the Bulge becomes the largest American battle of the war.

headline: V-2 hits the Rex cinema in Antwerp
detail: A rocket falls on a packed cinema during a matinee, killing 567 soldiers and civilians, the deadliest single V-2 strike.

headline: Malmedy massacre at the Baugnez crossroads
detail: Men of Kampfgruppe Peiper machine-gun captured American soldiers in a snowy field; 84 are killed.

headline: 'Nuts!': McAuliffe's answer at Bastogne
detail: Surrounded, the acting commander of the 101st Airborne replies to a German surrender demand with one word.

headline: Troopship Leopoldville torpedoed off Cherbourg
detail: A U-boat sinks the Belgian liner carrying reinforcements for the Bulge on Christmas Eve. 763 American soldiers die.

headline: Patton's tanks break through to Bastogne
detail: The 4th Armored Division opens a narrow corridor to the encircled town.

headline: Red Army encircles Budapest
detail: Soviet and Romanian troops close the ring around the Hungarian capital, trapping some 800,000 civilians.

headline: Operation Bodenplatte: the Luftwaffe's last great strike
detail: Hundreds of German fighters attack Allied airfields in Belgium and Holland. Germany loses about 300 aircraft and pilots it cannot replace.

headline: Four women hanged at Auschwitz for the revolt
detail: Roza Robota, Ala Gertner, Regina Safirsztajn and Estusia Wajcblum, who smuggled gunpowder to the Sonderkommando, are executed before the prisoners.

headline: US Sixth Army lands at Lingayen Gulf on Luzon
detail: Kamikazes strike the fleet, but about 68,000 troops land on the first day, on the same beaches Japan used in 1941.

headline: Soviet Vistula-Oder offensive begins
detail: From bridgeheads on the Vistula, Soviet fronts shatter the German line and advance some 500 kilometres to the Oder in three weeks.

headline: Soviet and Polish troops enter ruined Warsaw
detail: The left-bank city is a field of rubble, systematically dynamited since the Uprising. Almost nobody is left living there.

headline: Raoul Wallenberg detained by Soviet troops
detail: The Swedish diplomat who saved thousands of Budapest's Jews with protective passports is taken by the Red Army and never freed.

headline: SS force Auschwitz prisoners on death marches
detail: About 56,000 prisoners are marched west through snow. Thousands are shot or die of cold on the roads.

headline: Red Army reaches Auschwitz
detail: Soviet troops find about 7,000 prisoners still alive. At least 1.1 million people were murdered here, about a million of them Jews.

headline: First convoy crosses into China on the Ledo Road
detail: Trucks from Ledo in India cross the border at Wanting, reopening a land route to China. They reach Kunming on 4 February.

headline: Wilhelm Gustloff sunk with over 9,000 lives lost
detail: A Soviet submarine torpedoes the overloaded refugee ship in the icy Baltic, the deadliest ship sinking in history.

headline: Rangers and guerrillas free the Cabanatuan prisoners
detail: Behind Japanese lines on Luzon, a night raid rescues 489 prisoners of war and 33 civilians, many of them survivors of Bataan.

headline: Private Eddie Slovik executed for desertion
detail: He is the only American soldier shot for desertion since the Civil War.

headline: US troops reach Manila and free Santo Tomas
detail: A flying column of the 1st Cavalry Division frees about 3,700 civilian internees. The month-long battle for the city begins.

headline: The Big Three meet at Yalta
detail: Roosevelt, Churchill and Stalin agree occupation zones, Soviet entry into the war with Japan, and Poland's borders moved west.

headline: Operation Veritable opens the battle for the Rhineland
detail: British and Canadian troops attack through the flooded Reichswald forest toward the Rhine.

headline: Budapest falls after a 50-day siege
detail: The last defenders of Buda surrender. Tens of thousands of civilians have died in the siege.

headline: Allied bombers devastate Dresden
detail: In three raids over two days RAF and US bombers create a firestorm. A historians' commission later puts the dead at up to 25,000.

headline: Fourteenth Army crosses the Irrawaddy at Nyaungu
detail: Indian troops make one of the longest opposed river crossings of the war, opening the road to Meiktila.

headline: US paratroopers drop on Corregidor
detail: The fortress island where American resistance ended in 1942 is retaken in eleven days of fighting.

headline: US Marines land on Iwo Jima
detail: About 30,000 Marines land on the first day against some 21,000 defenders dug into tunnels.

headline: Flags raised on Mount Suribachi
detail: Marines raise a small flag in the morning; a larger one replaces it, photographed by Joe Rosenthal. The battle has a month to run.

headline: Los Banos internees rescued at dawn
detail: Paratroopers, Filipino guerrillas and amphibious tractors free 2,147 civilians from a Japanese camp south of Manila.

headline: Turkey declares war on Germany and Japan
detail: The largely symbolic declaration secures Turkey a seat at the founding conference of the United Nations.

headline: Egypt's prime minister assassinated
detail: Ahmad Mahir Pasha is shot in parliament after announcing that Egypt will declare war on the Axis.

headline: Battle of Manila ends
detail: The city is free but destroyed. About 100,000 Filipino civilians have died, many murdered by Japanese troops.

headline: RAF bombs The Hague's Bezuidenhout district by mistake
detail: Bombs aimed at V-2 launch sites fall on a residential quarter, killing about 500 people.

headline: Finland declares war on Germany
detail: The declaration is backdated to 15 September 1944; Finnish troops have been fighting the Germans in Lapland since the autumn.

headline: Indian 17th Division takes Meiktila
detail: A deep armoured thrust captures the Japanese supply hub in central Burma, cutting the communications of the armies at Mandalay.

headline: Americans seize the Ludendorff Bridge at Remagen
detail: Men of the 9th Armored Division cross the Rhine on a railway bridge the Germans failed to blow.

headline: Japan seizes control of French Indochina
detail: Japanese troops overthrow the Vichy French administration in a night of attacks. Thousands of French soldiers are killed or interned.

headline: Firebombing of Tokyo kills about 100,000
detail: B-29s drop incendiaries on the city's wooden districts overnight. A million people are made homeless.

headline: Hitler issues the 'Nero Decree'
detail: He orders the destruction of Germany's own industry and infrastructure. Albert Speer quietly works to frustrate it.

headline: Mandalay's Fort Dufferin falls
detail: After days of shelling the 19th Indian Division takes the old royal fort, completing the capture of Burma's second city.

headline: Arab League founded in Cairo
detail: Egypt, Iraq, Transjordan, Lebanon, Saudi Arabia and Syria sign its founding pact.

headline: Operation Varsity: airborne drop across the Rhine
detail: About 16,000 paratroopers and glider troops land east of the river near Wesel in the largest single-day airborne operation.

headline: Battle of Iwo Jima ends
detail: About 6,800 Americans and nearly all of the 21,000 Japanese defenders are dead.

headline: Last V-2 to hit Britain falls on Orpington
detail: Ivy Millichamp, 34, becomes the last civilian killed by enemy action in Britain.

headline: Americans land on Okinawa
detail: About 60,000 troops come ashore unopposed on the first day. The fighting inland will last 82 days.

headline: US troops find Ohrdruf camp
detail: The Buchenwald subcamp is the first Nazi camp entered by American forces. Eisenhower visits on 12 April and orders it documented.

headline: Battleship Yamato sunk
detail: On a one-way mission to Okinawa, the world's largest battleship is sunk by American carrier aircraft. About 3,000 of her crew die.

headline: Bonhoeffer, Canaris and Oster hanged at Flossenburg
detail: The theologian, the former Abwehr chief and his deputy are executed on Hitler's orders, weeks before the end.

headline: Buchenwald liberated
detail: As American troops arrive, the prisoners' underground takes over the camp. About 21,000 survivors are found, among them some 900 children.

headline: President Roosevelt dies
detail: He dies of a stroke at Warm Springs, Georgia. Harry S. Truman is sworn in as president.

headline: Polish tank crews free the women of Oberlangen
detail: The 1st Polish Armoured Division liberates a camp holding some 1,700 women soldiers of the Warsaw Uprising.

headline: British troops enter Bergen-Belsen
detail: They find some 60,000 prisoners, many dying of typhus and starvation, and thousands of unburied dead.

headline: Battle for Berlin begins
detail: Soviet guns open on the Seelow Heights. Some 2.5 million Soviet and Polish troops launch the final assault.

headline: United Nations conference opens in San Francisco
detail: Delegates of 50 nations begin drafting the Charter of a new world organisation.

headline: Mussolini shot by partisans
detail: Captured near Lake Como, he is executed with Clara Petacci. Their bodies are hung in Piazzale Loreto, Milan.

headline: American troops liberate Dachau
detail: The first concentration camp, opened in 1933, holds some 32,000 living prisoners.

headline: Operation Manna: food drops to the starving Dutch
detail: Under a local truce, RAF bombers drop food to the western Netherlands, where the Hunger Winter has killed some 20,000 people.

headline: Hitler kills himself in his Berlin bunker
detail: Soviet soldiers are fighting a few hundred metres away. Admiral Donitz is named his successor.

headline: Berlin surrenders
detail: General Weidling surrenders the city to the Red Army. German forces in Italy lay down their arms the same day.

headline: Indian troops enter Rangoon
detail: The Japanese have abandoned Burma's capital. The monsoon breaks over the advancing Fourteenth Army.

headline: German forces surrender at Luneburg Heath
detail: Troops in north-west Germany, the Netherlands and Denmark surrender to Field Marshal Montgomery.

headline: American troops reach Mauthausen
detail: In the Austrian camp and its subcamp Gusen, prisoners were worked to death in the granite quarries.

headline: Prague rises against the German garrison
detail: Czech citizens build barricades across the city and broadcast appeals for help.

headline: Germany signs unconditional surrender at Reims
detail: General Jodl signs at Eisenhower's headquarters at 02:41; the surrender takes effect the next night.

headline: Victory in Europe
detail: Crowds fill the streets of London, Paris and New York. Churchill broadcasts at 15:00.

headline: Setif: VE Day march turns to massacre in Algeria
detail: After riots kill about 100 Europeans, French forces and settler militias kill thousands of Algerians in weeks of reprisals.

headline: Channel Islands liberated
detail: British troops land in Guernsey and Jersey, ending five years of German occupation.

headline: Red Army enters Prague
detail: Soviet tanks reach the city as the last German resistance in Europe collapses. Moscow celebrates victory.

headline: Himmler kills himself in British custody
detail: Captured in disguise at a checkpoint, the SS chief bites a cyanide capsule during a medical examination at Luneburg.

headline: Marines take Shuri Castle on Okinawa
detail: The ancient castle at the heart of the Japanese defence line falls after weeks of slaughter on the surrounding ridges.

headline: Allies assume supreme authority over Germany
detail: In Berlin the four Allied commanders sign a declaration dividing the country into occupation zones.

headline: Chinese armies win the battle of West Hunan
detail: Japan's last major offensive in China, aimed at the airfield at Zhijiang, ends in defeat.

headline: Australians land at Brunei Bay in Borneo
detail: The 9th Australian Division comes ashore to retake oilfields and free prisoners in North Borneo.

headline: Scientists' Franck Report urges a demonstration of the bomb
detail: Chicago physicists warn against a surprise atomic attack on Japan and predict a nuclear arms race.

headline: African and colonial troops march in the Paris victory parade
detail: On the fifth anniversary of de Gaulle's appeal, units from North and West Africa parade down the Champs-Elysees.

headline: Organised resistance on Okinawa ends
detail: About 12,500 Americans have died, and more than 100,000 Japanese soldiers and Okinawan civilians.

headline: Victory parade in Red Square
detail: Soviet soldiers hurl captured German standards at the foot of Lenin's mausoleum in the rain.

headline: United Nations Charter signed
detail: Delegates of 50 nations sign the Charter in San Francisco. Poland, absent, will sign later as the 51st founding member.

headline: Czechoslovakia cedes Carpathian Ruthenia to the Soviet Union
detail: A treaty signed in Moscow moves the easternmost province into Soviet Ukraine, the first of many post-war border changes.

headline: Australians land at Balikpapan
detail: The last major Allied amphibious assault of the war goes ashore on the coast of Borneo.

headline: Britain votes in its first general election for ten years
detail: Ballots from servicemen overseas take three weeks to count. Results are declared on 26 July.

headline: Operation Rimau prisoners executed in Singapore
detail: Ten captured Australian and British commandos are beheaded weeks before the war ends.

headline: Trinity: the first atomic bomb is tested
detail: At 05:29 in the New Mexico desert a plutonium device explodes with the force of about 20,000 tons of TNT.

headline: Potsdam Conference opens
detail: Truman, Stalin and Churchill meet outside Berlin. On the 24th Truman tells Stalin of a powerful new weapon.

headline: Potsdam Declaration demands Japan's surrender
detail: The Allies warn Japan that the alternative is 'prompt and utter destruction'.

headline: Attlee's Labour Party wins a landslide
detail: Churchill leaves office. Clement Attlee returns to Potsdam as prime minister.

headline: Chinese troops retake Guilin
detail: The Guangxi city lost in November is recovered as Japanese forces pull back across southern China.

headline: Bomber crashes into the Empire State Building
detail: A B-25 lost in fog hits the 79th floor, killing 14 people.

headline: USS Indianapolis sunk by a Japanese submarine
detail: The cruiser had delivered parts of the Hiroshima bomb to Tinian. Of 1,195 crew, 879 die, many from sharks and exposure.

headline: Atomic bomb destroys Hiroshima
detail: At 08:15 a single bomb from the B-29 Enola Gay kills some 70,000 people at once. By year's end about 140,000 are dead.

headline: Soviet Union declares war on Japan
detail: Moscow tears up its neutrality pact as Soviet armies mass on the Manchurian border.

headline: London Charter defines crimes against humanity
detail: The Allies agree rules for an International Military Tribunal to try the major Nazi leaders at Nuremberg.

headline: Atomic bomb destroys Nagasaki
detail: At 11:02 a plutonium bomb kills some 40,000 people at once. About 74,000 are dead by the end of the year.

headline: Soviet armies invade Manchuria
detail: More than 1.5 million Soviet troops attack Japan's Kwantung Army on three fronts.

headline: China and the Soviet Union sign a treaty
detail: Chiang Kai-shek's government accepts Soviet rights in Manchuria in return for Stalin's recognition.

headline: Emperor Hirohito announces Japan's surrender
detail: At noon Japanese hear their emperor's voice for the first time. Britain celebrates VJ Day.

headline: Petain sentenced to death
detail: The Vichy leader is convicted of treason. De Gaulle commutes the sentence to life imprisonment.

headline: Sukarno proclaims Indonesian independence
detail: In Jakarta, nationalists declare a republic before the Dutch can return. Four years of war will follow.

headline: Viet Minh take Hanoi
detail: In the August Revolution, Ho Chi Minh's movement seizes power across northern Vietnam.

headline: Mao Zedong flies to Chongqing for talks
detail: Mao and Chiang Kai-shek negotiate for six weeks; civil war will resume within a year.

headline: MacArthur lands at Atsugi
detail: The Supreme Commander steps off his plane, corncob pipe in hand, to begin the occupation of Japan.

headline: Royal Navy returns to Hong Kong
detail: Admiral Harcourt's fleet sails into Victoria Harbour, ending three years and eight months of Japanese occupation.

headline: Japan signs the surrender aboard USS Missouri
detail: At 09:04 in Tokyo Bay Foreign Minister Shigemitsu signs. The Second World War is over.

headline: Ho Chi Minh proclaims Vietnam's independence
detail: In Hanoi's Ba Dinh Square he reads a declaration that opens with words from the American Declaration of Independence.
